author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Boston College linebacker Bodie Kahoun had movement in all of his extremities after suffering a serious injury during Friday night's game against Rutgers, the school said. Medical personnel immobilized Kahoun, placed him on a stretcher and moved him by ambulance to a local hospital for further evaluation.

The injury occurred in the second quarter after Kahoun tackled Rutgers running back Antwan Raymond. Players from both teams gathered nearby while trainers worked, and Kahoun gave a thumbs-up as he was carried from the field. Boston College's update offered an important initial sign, but the school did not announce a diagnosis or timetable.

Kahoun is in his first season with the Eagles after transferring from Notre Dame. He had recorded six tackles in the game before leaving. The episode shifted attention away from the score as players and spectators waited for information about his condition. Further testing will determine the extent of the injury and any next steps in his recovery; the initial statement should not be read as a complete medical assessment.
dek: Bodie Kahoun was taken to a hospital after being immobilized and carried from Friday night's game against Rutgers.
headline: Boston College linebacker has movement after serious injury
